body: This is the behavior of Esprima, so we would need to get it fixed there.

This is not an esprima/eslint bug, it is a node bug that they refuse to fix. See https://github.com/joyent/node/issues/6254. @wavded: Wrap your code in an IIFE to get the feature you want in a spec-compliant way.

@michaelficarra perhaps, IIFE is pretty ugly IMO just to get this functionality and if Node core peeps don't consider it a bug to fix (seems like CommonJS impl detail?) then it seems worth supporting.  Unfortunately ideals and practice don't always aline with one another :(
Then what's the proposal?  Ask esprima to have a node mode to work around the node bug? I don't see that happening.
From what I read, the node behavior isn't a bug, it's a design decision. I don't see any reason why we can't at least ask to support this.

But esprima is an ECMAScript parser that is supposed to parse all valid programs _and fail on invalid programs_. Node is allowing a syntactic superset of ECMAScript. esprima can't possibly parse it successfully while retaining its guarantees. The only way to do so would be to introduce a mode that parses the node superset. You might instead propose a "permissive" mode that always produces a parse tree, no matter how malformed the input is. I think that is more likely to be accepted (because it is not a moving target), yet it will be a lot of work.

I don't make it a habit to make requests specifying how my request should be implemented. I'd just ask for a way to allow this behavior and let the Esprima team decide if they want to support it, and if so, what makes most the most sense. If they don't want to support it, then we can go from there.
Acorn has an option to allow `return` statements outside from functions. Maybe this should be considered in #1126.

Why don't we allow a parser to be passed in? The only requirement is that it respects [the `Reflect.parse` API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Projects/SpiderMonkey/Parser_API). **edit:** From the CLI, we can just specify the name of a node module that's installed as a sibling.
We rely on more than just the parser API. See #1025.

Am I understanding correctly that currently esprima is considering the code in question invalid entirely and therefore eslint doesn't actually lint the file, and consequently there's no way to disable this as if it were an eslint rule violation?
Yes, esprima is correctly refusing to parse input that is not a JavaScript program.
No, that would affect all position-related information. Line number and ranges would be completely off.

It tried something similar to solve #892 (see [084aaaa](https://github.com/btmills/eslint/commit/084aaaa2d1851379645cd088cdbd14fd59eb67e2) on my fork for the code), except that it wrapped the parsed AST instead of the entire script. However, it required some hacks around locations when reporting. If someone can figure out how to wrap scripts without requiring hacks elsewhere, that might knock both of these issues out at the same time.
I think the right answer is to have the parser do it. Anything done outside the parser will be a hack.

@nzakas FYI the node wrapper actually just extends your first line as [shown here](https://github.com/joyent/node/blob/885f72105bf0b18007100550f131c85ca56536e0/src/node.js#L796) so it cleverly doesn't alter the line numbers. It's just some code that comes before your first code characters on the first line. It does add an extra line to the end but in practice that seems to not cause any problems.
It would affect the column numbers and location ranges.
@focusaurus we looked at this extensively. Adding additional code causes nontrivial issues for ESLint. We aren't theorizing about this, we tried it and found the problems.
